sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Our Heilbronn data is recent, so there is no city trend yet; the figures below are for weekdays and weekends in August and September 2026.

Heilbronn has adopted new street parking fees, the first since 2011 [1]. The council adopted a new fee ordinance on 30 April 2026, to take effect on 1 January 2027: a four-zone system with €1.00 per 20 minutes in the central Zone I, limited to one hour, and a €4 day ticket in Zone IV [0]. Resident permits, which the city had held back in 2022 [3], are to rise to €120 a year from the same date [2]. The change comes after years of small steps. In 2020 several streets in the northern centre were merged into one zone with Sunday charging [14], and in September 2020 one council group proposed cutting on-street parking in the northern centre by a third, a proposal for the budget talks rather than a decision [15]. On Karlstraße 60 spaces are being removed, with the city citing cyclist safety on school routes and new markings due from September 2026 [17]. A 2019 mobility concept had already set out the idea of fees graded by distance to the centre, with park-and-ride at transit stops [13].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
The big change in the garage market is on the edge of the centre. The city's utility, SWHN, opened a 643-space electric 'Quartiersgarage' in the new Neckarbogen district in May 2024, with 202 charge points and state funding of €2 million [6][7]. Next to it the Innovationspark has a 423-space garage with 200 charge points shared by nearby companies [9]. In our data the Neckarbogen garage stands at 16% on weekdays. SWHN raised the daily maximum at some of its garages from January 2024 [4], and the local paper reported that the private operator B+B had charged somewhat more since October 2025 [5].

SWHN's garages can now use number-plate recognition instead of paper tickets, with plate data deleted within 24 hours [10], and the new street ordinance counts phone-app payment as equal to the meter [11]. In 2021 the city was renewing its guidance system, from 8 to 12 garages, with the start reported as slipping into 2022 [12]. Two things could change demand in the centre: an investor's plans for a new Wollhaus centre, which are only plans [18], and the Galeria department store, one of 33 branches reported under review in July 2026 [19]. Investment in the education campus continues, with 15 new professorships planned [21].

sections.title: Operators, location, price and use
sections.text:
The centre's garages are cheap and quiet. Within a kilometre of the Marktplatz eight garages hold about 3,000 spaces at typically €2.50 an hour, and they average 22% on weekdays and 18% at weekends. B+B Parkhaus runs the Wollhaus, Harmonie and K3 garages at €2.50 and €18 a day, at 32%, 24% and 18% respectively. SWHN's Bollwerksturm garage, also €2.50, is at 15%, and the Stadtgalerie shopping-centre garage, with 660 spaces at €2.00, at 23%. The busiest central site is the small Lohtorstraße garage (44%), which is also the dearest, at €3.00.

The garages at the clinics, all run by Goldbeck, are cheaper at €1.50 an hour and €9 a day. They are busier on weekdays (up to 56% at Gesundbrunnen P3, with peaks reaching 100%) and almost empty at weekends. Overall the city's garages are 25% occupied on weekdays and only 15% at weekends, so there is spare capacity almost everywhere.
